description: Snowflake Scripting ASYNC (<statement>) and AWAIT ALL. The engine is single-threaded, so ASYNC runs its wrapped DML or CALL SYNCHRONOUSLY and AWAIT is a no-op - the observable RESULT is identical, only the concurrency is lost, which is why these tests assert effects rather than timing. Two ASYNC deletes each carrying a :bind run and leave their tables at five rows, and an ASYNC CALL runs the callee, which is the shape that would silently do nothing if ASYNC merely parsed. Converted 1:1 from scripting/ProceduralAsyncTest (now retired); the ten-row fixtures are built with one INSERT instead of the Java loop's twenty.

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE archive() RETURNS STRING LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ DECLARE thr INT DEFAULT 5; BEGIN ASYNC (DELETE FROM a1 WHERE x <= :thr); ASYNC (DELETE FROM a2 WHERE x <= :thr); AWAIT ALL; RETURN 'done'; END $$
SELECT x FROM a1 ORDER BY x
SELECT x FROM a2 ORDER BY x
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE ins(v INT) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO alog VALUES (:v); RETURN 1; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE caller() RETURNS STRING LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN ASYNC (CALL ins(42)); AWAIT ALL; RETURN 'ok'; END $$
